summary: Travel advance reimbursement misclassified as vendor invoice -> payment batch blocked
description:
Issue summary:
A travel advance reimbursement for contractor vendor code ADV-TRAVEL-2026 (claim TR-2026-0047) was ingested into AP as a vendor invoice (INV-TR-2026-1123) and therefore blocked by the vendor-payment validation workflow. Impact:
- $4,320 advance reimbursement stuck in AP queue; would normally be paid in next contractor payout cycle.
- Creates cashflow issues for contractor and increases CS churn risk.
- Manual intervention required to reclassify and release payment.
Environment:
- Production ingestion pipeline (claim-processor v2.7.1)
- Region: us-east
- Affected payment batch: CONTRACTOR-PAYOUT-2026-03-11

Steps to reproduce / observed behaviour:
1) Contractor submitted travel advance via expense UI on 2026-03-07 with attached receipt and bank details for reimbursement. Claim created: TR-2026-0047.
2) Ingestion pipeline picked up payload on 2026-03-09 and created an AP record labelled INV-TR-2026-1123 instead of an expense reimbursement record.
3) AP validation flagged mismatched GL code and put record into BLOCKED_PAYMENTS queue.
4) Finance attempted manual release but backend disallows payout until record type is invoice (manual override not permitted for contractor advances).

Logs / Evidence:
- Ingestion log excerpt (2026-03-09T03:12:45Z): claim_processor INFO "mapped claimant_bank_details -> ap.vendor_bank; record_type set = vendor_invoice"
- AP ledger export: INV-TR-2026-1123, amount 4320.00, status BLOCKED_PAYMENTS, note: "classification: vendor_invoice (auto)"
- Expense UI entry: TR-2026-0047 (attached PDF receipts, claimant id: contractor-1982)

2026-03-10 14:32 - Anika Patel (Ingestion eng): Found rule change deployed 2026-03-01 that modified bank_details handling. It promoted any record with bank details to vendor precedence during mapping. Possible cause.

2026-03-13 15:28 - Marcus Lee: Production backfill completed. INV-TR-2026-1123 reclassified -> TR-2026-0047 expense_reimbursement. Payment released to contractor via expedited ACH. Ticket updated with remediation steps below.
investigation:
Hypothesis: A change to the ingestion mapping (deployed 2026-03-01) increased precedence of vendor mapping when claimant_bank_details were present, causing expense claims with bank info to be misclassified as vendor invoices. Confirmed by tracing mapping rules and ingestion logs: rule 'bank_details_to_vendor' evaluated before 'expense_claim' rule for claims with 'advance' flag missing due to a UI variant used by contractors. Additional contributing factor: contractor mobile UI omitted explicit 'advance=true' flag for contractor-1982 due to legacy client app version 1.9.4.
Evidence:
- Deploy diff: claim-processor v2.6.9 -> v2.7.0 (rule reordering in mapping_config.yml)
- Ingestion logs show direct mapping decision path that assigned record_type = vendor_invoice when bank_details present and advance flag null.
Next steps taken:
- Performed targeted backfill to reclassify affected records in production (tested in staging first).
- Patched mapping rules to require explicit claim_type == 'vendor' to map to vendor_invoice, and ensure 'advance' boolean overrides vendor precedence.
- Created quick validation in claim ingestion to flag missing 'advance' boolean for contractor clients and route to manual review instead of automatic vendor mapping.
resolution:
Workaround / fix applied:
1) Production backfill executed 2026-03-13 15:00 UTC: reclassified 7 records in CONTRACTOR-PAYOUT-2026-03-* batches (including TR-2026-0047).
2) Payment for contractor-1982 released via expedited ACH. Finance confirmed funds posted 2026-03-13 16:45 UTC.
3) Mapping config rollback/patch: rule 'bank_details_to_vendor' demoted; now requires explicit claim_type == 'vendor' or confirmed vendor account_id. Patch deployed 2026-03-12 22:30 UTC (claim-processor v2.7.2).
4) Added validation: claims from mobile client < v1.10 now flagged for manual review if advance boolean missing.
5) Follow-up action created: FIN-REQ-2026-17 to run audit of ingestion-mapped vendor invoices vs expense claims for last 90 days.

Follow-up items / Owners:
- Ingestion team (Anika Patel): monitor ingestion metrics for misclassifications for 7 days, produce dashboard alert.
- Finance Ops (Jordan Myers): reconcile any remaining blocked payments and confirm contractor satisfaction.
- DevRel/Client SDK team: notify external contractor cohort to upgrade mobile client; add safeguard in mobile app to include explicit advance flag.
- Engineering: create unit-test guarding mapping order and add regression test in CI.

Status: Ticket moved to In Progress while monitoring; payment released and immediate impact resolved. Further monitoring and audit required.
